A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Alignment Hypothesis and DomainBed-IP/OOP study. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and retained equations, experiments, tables and figures can be matched despite expansion and relocation.

before.justification: v2 reports original five-dataset DG experiments, alignment and perceptual-similarity analyses, and additional backbone evaluations (Table 2, Figure 2 and Appendix B).

after.justification: v3 retains those experiments and adds original zero-shot comparisons, scratch-training results, prediction-transition counts and image-content analyses (Tables 1, 3–6 and 9; Figure 10).

M1.justification: The principal procedure retains cosine AlignmentScore, filtering below 0.15 and above 0.4, and the 0.21 IP/OOP threshold. Algorithm 1 formalizes the previously described retrieval-and-binning workflow. Alternative scores are evaluated as diagnostic comparisons without replacing the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate multi-source image classification on DomainNet, OfficeHome, PACS, TerraIncognita and VLCS, with LAION-400M used for pretraining/retrieval. New analyses reuse this coverage. OpenAI CLIP and DINOv2 backbone evaluations already appear in v2 Appendix B.4.

E2.justification: v3 adds OpenCLIP ZS throughout the aggregate and per-domain IP/OOP/All comparisons, supplying a direct reference without source finetuning that v2 lacks. Appendix B.6 also compares confidence-based and averaged scores against AlignmentScore. The existing fine-tuned comparators and oracle remain.

E3.justification: The original training and target-domain evaluation protocol is retained. New experimental designs include a perceptual-similarity split at 0.86, ResNet-50 training from scratch with MPA, paired zero-shot/CLIPood correctness analysis, and VisDiff sampling with AUC filtering plus OWLv2 object-size measurements. These supplement rather than replace existing settings.

E4.justification: New Appendices B.5–B.9 test alternative split criteria, confidence-based and combined scores, similarity to source images, learning without pretraining, and prediction changes after finetuning. Sections C.4–C.5 add contextual-distractor and object-size analyses. The earlier backbone, labeling-noise and distribution analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. The new softmax-confidence diagnostic in Appendix B.6 is an alternative predictive score, not uncertainty reporting for experimental estimates.

E6.justification: All matched fine-tuned benchmark scores remain unchanged. v3 adds zero-shot averages of 79.0 on IP, 48.1 on OOP and 71.5 on All, alongside scratch-training, alternative-score, prediction-transition and image-characterization results. It also corrects the prose claim of beating the IP oracle on three datasets to two, although a subsequent sentence still says three.

T1.justification: Appendix B.6 newly defines Calibrated AlignmentScore using the true-class softmax probability p(c), and considers averaging AlignmentScore with PerceptualSimilarityScore. These are limited diagnostic definitions; the original cosine definitions and DG assumptions remain unchanged, with no new theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The Alignment Hypothesis, IP/OOP framework and central claim of dependence on pretraining remain. v3 drops the conclusion's explicit prediction of similar findings for single-source finetuning and changes the contribution statement from a promised split release to a stated release.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations concerning forgetting of initially correct IP predictions, task-irrelevant pretraining captions, competing image context and object size, including the TerraIncognita exception. It motivates raw alignment through cross-dataset score comparability and clarifies that the analysis does not assume how alignment arose. These extend v2's primarily alignment-based interpretation.

D1.justification: v3 provides a stated Hugging Face dataset-release location and documents VisDiff sampling, selection thresholds and OWLv2 use. It removes v2 Appendix A.1's statement that code is zipped in the supplement. The original optimizer settings, method hyperparameters and GPU information remain unchanged; actual external resource availability cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations and discussion concerning domain contamination, subpopulation shifts and evaluation leakage, including Mayilvahanan et al. (2025), Dehdashtian et al. (2024) and Yu et al. (2024). ADDA, VisDiff and OWLv2 references are also added. These broaden context without substantially redefining the central research positioning.

P1.justification: v3 introduces an explicit Discussion section and pseudocode explanation, converts algorithm descriptions from bullets to prose, condenses protocol and results passages, and updates publication and affiliation formatting. The main section sequence and much of the original exposition remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds diagnostic figures, comparison tables, confusion matrices and a multi-page VisDiff table, while expanding benchmark tables with zero-shot rows. Figure 2's panels are exchanged, dataset-statistics displays move to the appendix, and many retained plots are reproduced at substantially higher resolution.

improvement.justification: v3 addresses an important validation gap by adding same-backbone zero-shot comparisons and paired prediction counts, making the gains and forgetting from source finetuning directly assessable (Table 1; Tables 5–6). Alternative-score controls substantially strengthen the benchmarking rationale, while sharper figures and a stated dataset-release location improve inspectability and reuse. The scratch comparison also changes architecture, uncertainty remains unreported, and the code-supplement statement disappears. These limitations do not outweigh the substantial gain in evidence addressing the paper's central question.
